newsitem.title: RUSSIA: City of Moscow to get $200 mln syndicated credit.
newsitem.headline: City of Moscow to get $200 mln syndicated credit.

text.p: The City of Moscow is preparing to sign a $200 million three-year syndicated credit agreement with about 30 banks on June 10, the head of the foreign investment department at the Mayor's office said on Thursday.
"It is the first time that a Russian city has received a syndicated credit," Yuri Usaty told Reuters.
The credit, lead by WestMerchant Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Societe Generale, will be granted at 350 basis points over LIBOR rate, he said.
The banks have a call option each year, he said.
The credit coincides with this week's launch of a Eurobond by Moscow, making it also the first Russian non-sovereign entity issuing a Eurobond.
The larger than planned $500 million three-year bond was said to be tightly priced to yield 315 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
